title: 1989 AHSME Problem 17
statement: The perimeter of an equilateral triangle exceeds the perimeter of a square by \(1989\) cm. The length of each side of the triangle exceeds the length of each side of the square by \(d\) cm. The square has perimeter greater than \(0.\) How many positive integers are not possible values for \(d?\)

solutions.text:
If the square has side \(s,\) the triangle has side \(s+d.\) The perimeter condition gives \[ 3(s+d)-4s=1989, \] so \(s=3d-1989.\) The condition \(s\gt0\) is equivalent to \(d\gt663.\) Thus the positive integers \(1\) through \(663\) are precisely the impossible values.

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Let the square’s side length be \(s\)
Translate the positive-perimeter condition into a strict inequality for \(d\)
